harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an SSH CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca, ed25519), signed node1's ed25519 host public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals: node1, 10.100.247.10, localhost; valid 10y), and configured sshd via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-host-cert.conf (HostCertificate directive). Diagnosed and fixed an SELinux mislabel (tmp_t instead of sshd_key_t) that silently prevented sshd from loading the cert, then restarted sshd. Verified end-to-end that an SSH client whose known_hosts contains only the CA's public key (`@cert-authority * <ca-pubkey>`, no pinned host key) connects successfully and explicitly reports "Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate," while an empty known_hosts file fails — proving trust flows from the CA, not key pinning. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until the node returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd active, the host certificate config intact, and CA-based client trust working post-reboot. All test client keys/known_hosts files were cleaned up afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/sshd baseline and existing host keys
Captured pre-change boot_id and sshd active state
Generated SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca on node1
Signed the ed25519 host public key as a host certificate with ssh-keygen -s, principals node1/10.100.247.10/localhost, 10y validity
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-host-cert.conf with HostCertificate directive; validated with sshd -t
Diagnosed SELinux tmp_t mislabel preventing sshd from loading the cert via journalctl, fixed with chcon/semanage fcontext to sshd_key_t, restarted sshd
Verified via live SSH client test (only @cert-authority line in known_hosts, no pinned host key) that connection succeeds and explicitly matches the CA-signed certificate
Verified failure case with empty known_hosts to confirm trust is CA-derived, not incidental
Cleaned up test client keys and authorized_keys entries
Captured pre-restart boot_id/service baseline, issued systemctl reboot on node1, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified sshd active, host certificate config intact, and CA-based client trust working post-reboot
Cleaned up second round of test artifacts

evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated ed25519 CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca with proper permissions

evidence.requirement: Host presents a certificate signed by the CA
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed the host's ed25519 pubkey producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with correct principals and signing CA fingerprint

evidence.requirement: sshd configured to present the certificate
evidence.summary: sshd_config.d drop-in added, config validated, sshd -T confirms hostcertificate directive active, sshd remains active

evidence.requirement: Root-caused and fixed why the cert wasn't actually offered
evidence.summary: journalctl revealed sshd could not load the cert file; ls -Z showed SELinux tmp_t mislabel; chcon/semanage fixed to sshd_key_t; sshd restart loaded cleanly with no errors

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA (no host-key pinning) connects successfully
evidence.summary: SSH client with known_hosts containing only '@cert-authority * <ca-pubkey>' connected and logged 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'; control test with empty known_hosts failed, proving trust is CA-derived
Captured boot_id 31949c21-52ad-47af-bdbe-893352fd509b, sshd active, cert config intact before reboot
systemctl reboot issued in background; exec stream closed as node went down, confirming the restart was actioned

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot (connection timed out twice), then returned with new boot_id 125246ae-2f4e-4c2e-bbf5-39804ae05865 and fresh uptime, differing from pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of services and CA-based trust
evidence.summary: sshd active and listening, host certificate config intact with correct SELinux labels post-reboot; fresh client trust test with only the CA in known_hosts succeeded, printing POST_REBOOT_TRUST_OK and 'matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'
